entries.proposition: Study population: TOP trial randomized extremely low birth weight preterm infants to higher or lower haemoglobin thresholds, with thresholds set by postnatal age and respiratory support.
entries.snippet: The TOP trial randomized preterm infants of birth weight 1000 g or less and gestational age between 22 weeks 0 days and 28 weeks 6 days within 48 hours of birth to receive RBC transfusions at higher or lower Hgb thresholds.

experimental_context.endpoint: cerebral and mesenteric tissue oxygen saturation; death or neurodevelopmental impairment at 22-26 months

entries.proposition: Data attrition: of 140 transfused infants only 101 had valid pre and post NIRS data; 73 events lacked pre-transfusion and 26 post-transfusion NIRS.
entries.snippet: When restricted to transfusions with both valid pretransfusion and posttransfusion NIRS data, there remained 101 infants with a total of 237 transfusion events captured.

entries.proposition: Primary result: cerebral saturation rose 4.8 points (low threshold) and 2.7 points (high threshold) after transfusion, mesenteric 6.7 and 5.6, with no change in peripheral saturation and no difference between threshold groups.
entries.snippet: Mean Csat change in the lower–Hgb threshold group was 4.8% (95% CI, 2.7%-6.9%) compared to 2.7% (95% CI, 1.2%-4.2%) in the higher–Hgb threshold group, while mean change in Msat was 6.7% (95% CI, 2.4%-11.0%) vs 5.6% (95% CI, 2.7%-8.5%).

entries.proposition: Exploratory outcome: the number of transfusions with pre-transfusion Csat below 50 percent was associated with death or NDI (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.08-5.41, P = .03); 36 of 97 had the outcome.
entries.snippet: Significant prognostic factors for NDI or death included the total number of transfusions with mean pretransfusion cerebral saturation less than 50% (odds ratio, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.08-5.41; P = .03), total days of mechanical ventilation, and mean study Hgb (Table 2), with a similar c statistic of 0.73.

entries.proposition: The authors label the outcome analysis as hypothesis-generating and exploratory.
entries.snippet: In pursuing our secondary, hypothesis-generating objective to explore the association of cerebral NIRS measures and other clinical factors with the adverse composite outcome of NDI or death,24 we used different analytical approaches to interrogate this complex question.25

entries.proposition: Higher mean haemoglobin was associated with the adverse outcome, which the authors attribute to sicker infants receiving extra transfusions outside protocol.
entries.snippet: Although Hgb 12.5 mg/dL or greater was an associated variable from the CART analysis, infants with Hgb 12.5 mg/dL or greater received more transfusions outside of study protocol than other infants and may have intentionally been kept at a higher Hgb level due to severity of illness, inherently placing them at higher risk for adverse outcomes.

entries.proposition: Confounders of NIRS beyond haemoglobin are acknowledged (patent ductus, blood pressure, carbon dioxide, hypoxia, sepsis, cardiac output, vascular resistance).
entries.snippet: Another mechanistic consideration is that after a transfusion, a corresponding change in cardiac output or end-organ vascular resistance may impact NIRS measures beyond the effect of an increase in Hgb.
